events.address: 4th and Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20565
events.description: Old Glory, reimagined: artists transform our flag over the centuries. Across generations, the Stars and Stripes has inspired pride, protest, and profound artistic expression. From battlefields to modern cultural movements, our flag's journey through art reveals a nation constantly redefining itself. This installation features some 30 artworks from the late 1800s to present day, tracing how the meaning of the US flag has evolved over time. It explores what the flag represents and how people connect with it. You’ll find paintings, prints, and photographs by renowned artists like Gordon Parks, Childe Hassam, Dorothea Lange, Jasper Johns, and Faith Ringgold.

events.title: Bison: Standing Strong
events.address: 10th St. & Constitution Ave., NW, Washington, DC 20560
events.description: Explore the remarkable story of bison. These iconic animals shaped North American landscapes for more than 100,000 years and anchored Indigenous lifeways for generations. Pushed to the brink of extinction in the 19th century, bison survived thanks to dedicated conservation efforts. Today, they stand strong as an enduring symbol of survival and resilience. The Bison: Standing Strong exhibit invites you into this incredible journey. Explore a full-sized bull bison specimen, the six-foot-wide skull of an ancient bison ancestor, an immersive soundscape, multimedia, cutting-edge scientific research, and Native objects and stories shared in collaboration with community members. Experience the deep history of America’s national mammal and discover the hopeful future being built for generations to come.

events.title: Bronze Bison: Exhibit
events.address: 10th St. & Constitution Ave., NW, Washington, DC 20560
events.description: More than 100 years ago, real bison grazed outside the Smithsonian Castle building. Bison are returning in a bold new way! Three larger-than-life bronze bison, created by sculptor Gary Staab, find a permanent home outside the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History. These towering sculptures of a bull, cow, and calf are at 125 percent scale and modeled after taxidermy specimens seen at the Smithsonian between 1888 and 1957. The original bison diorama introduced generations of visitors to an animal and a prairie landscape they had never seen and helped spark the bison conservation movement. The new bison bronzes will welcome visitors from around the world and celebrate America’s national mammal. Gift of Naoma Tate and the family of Hal Tate.

events.title: Civil War History in Oakton and Vienna
events.description: Greater Oakton Community Association invites history enthusiasts to join a narrated historic bus tour led by acclaimed local historian Jim Lewis on from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. Please arrive at 9:00 a.m. at Oakton Community Park at 2841 Hunter Mill Road (next to the old schoolhouse and roundabout) for Jim Lewis's opening comments, then board the bus for departure by 9:30 a.m. The tour will end at 1:00 p.m. This 3.5-hour journey spans Fairfax County's history from its formation in 1742 through the early 1900s, focusing on sites primarily on or just off Hunter Mill Road. Participants hear stories of where the old mills and roads were located and learn about famed military figures (particularly from the Civil War era) and colorful residents who graced the area. Numerous period photographs support the narrative, bringing history to life. Walking requirements are minimal, although one segment involves going down a slight grassy decline. The tour runs rain or shine. Snacks and water are included. Cost is $45 per seat. In the event of cancellation, refunds are provided if a replacement is found for the seat; a wait list is maintained for this purpose. There are 23 seats on the bus. Special "Event Pricing" is offered for the award-winning "Danger Between the Lines" DVD and tour-related illustrated books, available for purchase with cash only. Narrated Historic Bus Tour with Jim Lewis combines local history education, community connection, and immersive storytelling in Fairfax County, Virginia. Questions? Email contact@greateroakton.com . events.title: Entertainment Nation
events.address: 14th Street and Constitution Avenue, N.W., Washington, DC 20560
events.description: Entertainment has the power to captivate, inspire and transform us. It brings us together. We share it when we spontaneously recite lines from a favorite movie, dance to the same groove or recreate a national sports moment on a neighborhood street. It can also spur critical conversations, expose divides, and foster important historical change. Through the National Museum of American History’s extraordinary collection of theater, music, sports, movie and television objects, the exhibition features a powerful, ever-changing selection of objects and interactive experiences. Through the objects and their stories, the exhibition explores how, for more than 150 years, entertainment has provided a forum for important national conversations about who we are, and who we want to be.

events.description: Friends Gather Here: A Legacy of Two Communities at Woodlawn explores the powerful history of Quaker families who came to Woodlawn to establish an antislavery community rooted in equality and nonviolence. Through innovative farming and free labor, they sought to demonstrate an alternative to slavery in Virginia, settling alongside a small, established free Black community already living in the area. This exhibit examines the parallel lives, shared aspirations, and evolving relationships between these neighboring communities. As part of the Virginia 250th commemoration, Friends Gather Here invites us to reflect on this quiet revolution and examine our nation’s foundational ideals. On View: June 27 – December 30, 2026 Admission: Free (with suggested donation)

In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness will span three floors and 300,000 square feet, featuring 250 significant objects, including the desk Jefferson used to draft the Declaration of Independence. Another noteworthy artifact is the only surviving ship of the early U.S. Navy, the gunboat Philadelphia . This National Historic Landmark helped stall British forces and now will undergo an on-site conservation to preserve it for future generations. Visitors and online audiences can engage with both the triumphs and challenges of America’s journey through a year-long series of dynamic programs, from hands-on activities and theatrical performances to educational tools and virtual field trips for classrooms across the country. The museum's Semiquincentennial exhibitions and events begin in the spring of 2026, welcoming all Americans to reflect on the enduring and sometimes delayed or denied promises that surround the ongoing pursuit of life, liberty and happiness.

events.title: Miguel Braceli: UNBURIAL (exhibition)
events.address: St. John's College, 60 College Avenue, Annapolis, MD 21401
events.description: Unburial treats absence as a site for learning and reflection. The void left by the Liberty Tree becomes more than metaphor: an art intervention transforms it into a place to be repurposed and reclaimed through rituals and celebrations that probe what freedom means today. On the front lawn, where the Liberty Tree once stood, the artist Miguel Braceli has installed a 40'-diameter circle of cemetery vases filled with common wildflowers. It calls attention to the tree's absence and reclaims it as a tree for all people, not just the privileged and elite (e.g., the Sons of Liberty and the four Annapolis signers of the Declaration of Independence). In the museum, Braceli, with the help of a team of fabricators, created three enormous murals and two other works. The murals perform an autopsy of the tree. The largest multiplies the tulip poplar's distinctive leaf shape across a 33'-long wall in a wind-swept swirl of energy (the leaves were made from stencils of the Liberty Tree scion's actual leaves). A second mural abstracts the tree's tangled root system into a water-bearing drawing (using PVC tubing) that sprouts purple carnations. The third mural's subject is the tree's massive trunk, which was cut to pieces in 1999, with much of the wood later finding commemorative as Liberty Tree guitars, conference tables, and bible boxes. Onto nine chalkboards, Braceli has mounted nine pieces of raw wood, each supporting live orchids. What can we learn anew from this tree?, it seems to ask. The two other works urge us to turn away from nation-state identities and to look and listen more closely to nature. A sculptural ear is mounted onto the red silhouette of a rose petal, borrowed from the work of Columbia-born, Venezuela-based artist Roberto Obregoń. Nearby, a flag of yellow roses hangs from a flagpole that has been fabricated from a branch. Admission & Hours Free & open to the public Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Open Friday, 12 to 7:30 p.m. Parking

events.title: Shifting Boundaries: Perspectives on American Landscapes
events.address: Jefferson Drive at 12th St., SW, Washington, DC
events.description: American painters Willard Metcalf, Dwight Tryon, Winslow Homer, and Abbott Thayer created profoundly beautiful views of the New England landscapes where they lived and worked. These paintings largely depict that environment as timeless and static. Shifting Boundaries looks at these works from a new angle by engaging a multiplicity of voices and viewpoints to explore what these paintings can tell us about changes to this region both past and present. As Shifting Boundaries reveals, the views these artists created of pasturelands in Massachusetts and of seascapes in Maine were transforming even as these artists recorded them. This reshaping of landscapes has only accelerated in the century since Metcalf, Tryon, Homer, and Thayer depicted them. Shifting Boundaries pilots a new mode of collaborative curatorial practice. NMAA Lunder Curator of American Art Diana Greenwold , curatorial assistant Mary Mulcahy , and interpretation specialists Liz Gardner and Amy Freesun partnered with Lauren Brandes (Smithsonian Gardens), Dennis Chestnut (Groundwork Anacostia River DC), Jerome Foster II (Waic Up), Elizabeth James-Perry (Aquinnah Wampanoag artist), Lorette Picciano (Rural Coalition), Stephanie Toothman (National Park Service), and Melinda Whicher (Smithsonian Gardens) to develop the themes for this exhibition, select works of art, and write object labels. The group’s perspectives, drawn from their individual areas of professional expertise and their own personal experiences, allow us to see new details in these stunning works of art. The landscapes become invitations to explore a century of human impact on New England land and water, the erasure of indigenous histories, and the environmental changes that are altering this region today.

events.title: We Make History
events.description: As the nation commemorates 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence, "We Make History" explores how history happens, is preserved and shared. In Washington, D.C. and places around the country, many people were quietly keeping the records, building the collections, and developing the skills that would create America’s historical narrative. These community-based stories serve as the building blocks for 250 years of American history. Using the country’s anniversary as a milestone, the museum uses its community driven practice to celebrate local civic engagement and encourage local history keeping. This exhibition is a tribute to celebrating our communities and making possible a better understanding of our shared past. These stories are important to marking the Semiquincentennial because they help show the legacy of how people make history one act, one document, one story at a time. By bringing these stories to the forefront in 2026, the exhibit inspires the next generation to keep and share their own stories and records to add to America’s historical narrative. We Make History has an anticipated opening date of May 30, 2026.

events.description: Attend In-Person Attend Online Please join the Middle East Policy Forum, in partnership with the Sigur Center for Asian Studies, on November 3 to welcome Mohammed Soliman, author of West Asia: A New American Grand Strategy in the Middle East. Dr. Alyssa Ayres, Dean of the Elliott School of International Affairs, will deliver opening remarks. Mohammed Soliman argues in his book that it is time for the United States to move decisively away from nation-building and get back to the business of order-building. To do so will require zooming out, in both geographical and historical terms, to build a new regional order across ‘West Asia’ – from the Middle East to South Asia, connecting Europe to the Indo-Pacific via the Mediterranean and Red Seas. Working with India, Italy, Greece, France, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Japan, the UK, and the United Arab Emirates, among others, he shows how the United States could lock in a new balance of power in the Eurasian supercontinent to offset Chinese and Russian efforts to disrupt the status quo and create a rival system. This new strategy rests on three layered coalitions — geostrategic, hard-power, and geo-technological — that together can anchor a stable order stretching from the Mediterranean to the Indian Ocean. But this will require a fundamental shift in U.S. grand strategy, with ‘West Asia’ at its core. events.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh? Film Screening
events.description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California, was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when a Palestinian American, Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite clear evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. Unfolding like a detective thriller, the film weaves archival footage, firsthand testimony, and new reporting to expose the violent fundamentalist networks behind the attack and the institutional failures that protected them. As the investigation deepens, the story widens to reveal how the extremist ideology that fueled Odeh’s murder did not disappear - it evolved, gaining traction and legitimacy in the modern political landscape. Directed by SMPA Professors Jason Osder and William Lafi Youmans, a Jewish American and a Palestinian American, Who Killed Alex Odeh? is both a gripping cold-case pursuit and a timely examination of political violence, asking what it means when acts of terror go unresolved, and how justice denied continues to shape the world we live. The screening will be held on November 3 at 6 p.m. in the MPA 5th Floor Studio.

events.description: A multidisciplinary showcase from the artists and scholars of the full-time faculty and staff at the Corcoran School of the Arts & Design. A Gift In Motion loosely draws from Robin Wall Kimmerer’s book The Serviceberry which uplifts Indigenous frameworks of the natural world to advance the possibilities in collectivity, reciprocity, and the mindset of abundance. events.title: BME Department Seminar
events.description: Join the Department of Biomedical Engineering for their upcoming seminar featuring Dr. Simiao Niu, an assistant professor at Rutgers University! He will be presenting "Battery-free Wireless Bioelectronic Network for Effective Chronic Disease Management." Abstract: 60% of the US population live with at least one chronic disease. These diseases and associated comorbidities are now the leading causes of death. Effective management of complex chronic diseases requires body-wide, long-term, accurate, and continuous monitoring of multiple physiological signals from wearable devices to precisely determine the pathological state. These wearable physiological signal monitoring can dramatically reduce the demand of physician visiting and increase patients’ engagement and treatment adherence rate. Although wearable bioelectronic devices have shown huge potential in chronic disease management, existing technology still mostly relies on rigid chip components, where the interface between chips and skin/tissue has been a bottleneck that limits the system performance (noise, robustness etc). To address these challenges, my group's research has been involved in the exploration of rational system design concepts, material and device fabrication innovation, tailored algorithms, and energy harvesting to enable a closed-loop wireless bioelectronic network that targets next-generation chronic disease management. In this talk, I will discuss my group's efforts in building this technology platform.

events.title: Camp One Heartland
events.description: Camp One Heartland is a solo exhibition by Tye DuSold-O’Connor archiving documentation of one of the world’s first nonprofit summer camps designated to supporting and empowering youth affected by HIV and AIDS, eventually transforming into a vital beacon of safety, liberation and eutopia for LGBTQ+ youth across the country. After its inaugural session in the summer of 1993 and many more held at different campsites across the country, Camp One Heartland found its permanent residence in Willow River, Minnesota. Over the next three decades it broadened its reach to provide summer camp sessions for youth experiencing housing instability, LGBTQ+ youth, and specifically trans youth. Tye attended Camp One Heartland as both a camper in 2022 and a counselor in 2024, and found these experiences indescribably transformative to them and their queer identity. Quite suddenly, Camp One Heartland shut down permanently in the fall of 2024 due to financial issues. Former campers, counselors and staff have been unable to return to the site since. While camp counseling in the summer of 2024, Tye took hundreds of photos of the camp, its people, and its experiences. These serve as some of the last images taken during the lifetime of Camp One Heartland. events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.

events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. events.title: Demo-ing, Sampling, Lip-Syncing: Commercial Misogynoir in Post-Disco EDM
events.description: Join the GW Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies (WGSS) Program for an exciting talk from Visiting Assistant Professor Eva Pensis! Across the late 20th century, the popular music industry faced a series of scandals in live performance with the widespread use of lip-syncing. Following the advent of recorded sound, the commercial use of lip-sync in the popular music industry sought to divide the recorded performance from the performer with the aim of controlling both, most often eliding the visual presence of African American musicians while profiting from their sonic contributions. Framed by the media theorist Moya Bailey's concept of "misogynoir," this presentation considers the case of Black Box, an Italian post-disco house music band from the 1980s who stole and misattributed the vocal demos of Martha Wash (a noted musician and vocalist from The Weather Girls and Two Tons o’ Fun) for their debut album. The ensuing crisis of representation that lip-syncing indexes forms the basis for this talk's investigation into the popular music industry's predation on African American women's song following the infamous demolition of disco and the digital quest to strip sound from song. RSVP online.

Humanities in Asia: Going Beyond Make-Do-the Reshaping of a Chinese Operatic Tradition in Taiwan
events.description: Kunqu, a 600-year-old form of Chinese opera known for its poetic lyrics and refined singing, was among the first Chinese art forms UNESCO recognized as a "Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity" in 2001. The story of how Kunqu survived the political upheavals of the twentieth century runs not only through state-sponsored troupes in China but also through communities of devoted amateur singers, known as quyou (曲友), who carried the tradition to Taiwan. This talk follows these enthusiasts from their roots in Mainland China to their postwar lives in Taiwan, where they kept Kunqu alive through informal singing gatherings long before it was celebrated as world heritage. When cultural exchanges across the Taiwan Strait reopened, amateurs and professionals on both sides began collaborating on performances, training, preservation, and documentation, turning a private pastime into a shared project of heritage-making. Drawing on the experiences of Taiwan-based practitioners, the talk shows how this cross-strait collaboration reshaped Kunqu as a heritage for Sinophone audiences and how a common love for an art form built networks that reached beyond politics while still raising questions about cultural identity. Free lunch will be offered at this talk. Doors will open no sooner than 15 minutes before the start time. events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.description: Sophia Bush has always understood the power of stories. She’s seen it in the connection millions of viewers have had to the women she’s played on-screen—Dr. Sam Griffith on “Good Sam” and Dr. Cass Beckman on “Grey’s Anatomy,” Detective Erin Lindsay on “Chicago P.D.,” and the iconic Brooke Davis on “One Tree Hill.” She’s seen it in her activism, where speaking truth to inequality and power has prompted real change. And she’s seen it in her personal life, when her experiences and opinions have been distorted to drive clicks and create drama. She also offers sides of herself not often seen: the lifelong learner, the friend, the adventurer. And I Will Tell You Mine is an account of becoming, un-becoming, and becoming again to return home to our truest selves. events.title: The Alternate Routes
events.description: The Alternate Routes remind us that "we are how we treat each other, and nothing more." Their breakout 2005 album Good and Reckless and True launched a career of relentless touring and craft refinement across multiple label releases. Their anthem "Nothing More" propelled the band into new ears, featured prominently in the 2014 Winter Olympics and on NCIS. "Somewhere in America," a poignant conversation about gun violence, earned them a 2016 Independent Music Award and a White House visit. The band has collaborated with Patti Griffin, director Lisa Cholodenko, and guitarist Carl Broemel of My Morning Jacket, performing on The Late Late Show, Late Night with Conan O'Brien, and NPR's Mountain Stage. Pete Muller, a critically acclaimed songwriter and pianist, brings his genre-spanning blend of roots, rock, soul, and pop alongside his band The Kindred Souls (Eric Donnelly on guitar, Martha McDonnell on violin, Skip Ward on bass, Andy Mac on drums). His new album One Last Dance, recorded at Peter Gabriel's Real World Studios and featuring Grammy-winner Allison Russell and SistaStrings, showcases Muller's dynamic range and heartfelt approach. His festival slots span Telluride to Montreux, and he's toured with Jimmy Webb and Livingston Taylor. Onstage, Muller's passion and chemistry deliver unforgettable performances. Jammin' Java welcomes both acts to Fairfax County, Virginia.

events.title: Unfossilizing African Art
events.description: Presented after extensive research, this exhibition recontextualizes African material culture objects held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. Image: Once Known Mende carver [Mende, Sierra Leone], Sowei, 19th-20th century, wood, varnish, 16 H x 10 W x 10 D in. Gift of Stephen A. Spear, 1975 (P.75.2.30)

events.title: A Gift in Motion
events.description: A multidisciplinary showcase from the artists and scholars of the full-time faculty and staff at the Corcoran School of the Arts & Design. A Gift In Motion loosely draws from Robin Wall Kimmerer’s book The Serviceberry which uplifts Indigenous frameworks of the natural world to advance the possibilities in collectivity, reciprocity, and the mindset of abundance. These are anti-capitalist models and theories that provide insight into the systems of power we negotiate, but also offer a lens on how we individually move through our daily lives—together—through historically fraught landscapes. A keen reminder that working with, for, and because of each other remains the most human motivation, even while we are inundated with narratives that suggest otherwise. Within the walls of the academy, frameworks of artistic and creative knowledge are often dismissed, as are Indigenous methodologies and community-focused perspectives that center human engagement, oral and craft-based practices, and unquantifiable research. A personal experience. A feeling. Abstraction. And yet, for centuries, within the walls of art schools exist myriad economies of imagination that are anchored in the sharing of diverse creative knowledge and articulated in what we make, write, perform, dance, build, conserve, collect, display, speak, and think. events.title: Camp One Heartland
events.description: Camp One Heartland is a solo exhibition by Tye DuSold-O’Connor archiving documentation of one of the world’s first nonprofit summer camps designated to supporting and empowering youth affected by HIV and AIDS, eventually transforming into a vital beacon of safety, liberation and eutopia for LGBTQ+ youth across the country. After its inaugural session in the summer of 1993 and many more held at different campsites across the country, Camp One Heartland found its permanent residence in Willow River, Minnesota. Over the next three decades it broadened its reach to provide summer camp sessions for youth experiencing housing instability, LGBTQ+ youth, and specifically trans youth. Tye attended Camp One Heartland as both a camper in 2022 and a counselor in 2024, and found these experiences indescribably transformative to them and their queer identity. Quite suddenly, Camp One Heartland shut down permanently in the fall of 2024 due to financial issues. Former campers, counselors and staff have been unable to return to the site since. While camp counseling in the summer of 2024, Tye took hundreds of photos of the camp, its people, and its experiences. These serve as some of the last images taken during the lifetime of Camp One Heartland. Artist Bio: Tye DuSold-O’Connor is a multimedia artist studying Fine Art and Psychology whose work revolves around trans experience, identity and culture. events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.

events.title: Courage, Leadership, and Lessons from the Front Lines
events.description: Join us for an engaging discussion about leadership, service, and what it takes to remain steadfast when the stakes are at their highest. Join us for a compelling conversation with Steven Sund, author of Courage Under Fire, and Renn Cannon, author of Eyes on the Rose City, as they share firsthand insights from careers spent navigating some of the most challenging moments in law enforcement, public safety, and national security. Drawing from their books and professional experiences, Sund and Cannon will discuss leadership under pressure, decision-making in uncertain and rapidly evolving situations, and the personal and professional challenges that come with serving in high-stakes environments. They will also explore the importance of preparation, resilience, accountability, and courage when circumstances demand difficult decisions. They will also discuss why education must be a continuing commitment, not just a one-time milestone. In high-stakes professions, leaders and practitioners must continually study evolving threats, examine lessons from critical incidents, challenge assumptions, and translate experience into stronger judgement, preparedness, and decision-making. The webinar will offer students, professionals, and anyone interested in homeland security and public safety an opportunity to hear directly from two experienced practitioners and authors. events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. events.description: For Freedoms presents artist and educator Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY which centers on Ethiopian journalist and author Baalu Girma’s controversial 1984 Amharic novel Oromay, written under the Derg regime and banned shortly after its publication. Drawing on Gottesman’s deep engagement with the novel, NIGHT AND DAY considers how artists create, communicate, and sustain cultural memory within and against conditions of censorship, political repression, and state violence. The exhibition extends beyond the gallery through a library of banned books, a self-guided workshop station that invites visitors to respond to censorship through writing and drawing, and a public conversation on how artists sustain creative practice amid sociopolitical pressure.

events.title: Meet Pacific Prep: Free One-on-One Conversations for Families in Bethesda
events.description: The Admissions Team is coming to North Bethesda on Thursday, November 5, and we would love to sit down with you and your family. Pacific Preparatory is a Cognia-accredited online K-12 school. Every student learns through 1:1 live instruction that is built around that child, rather than asking the child to fit a school environment. Families can enroll full-time, add a single course, or work with our tutors for academic support, test prep, and enrichment. Our small team of real people takes the time to get to know each student well. We tend to be a good fit for students who have not been well served by traditional school. That includes kids with learning differences, kids who need more flexibility in how and when they learn, and kids who are ready to move faster than their classroom allows. If your child is bright but struggling, or capable but unhappy, we would be glad to see how we could help. We are offering free 20-minute, in-person conversations, with no cost and no obligation. You are welcome to come with questions, or just to tell us about your child and see whether we might be a good fit. events.title: Mental Reset: Sound Bath + Reiki : Thursday Evenings in Falls Church
events.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
events.description: Thursday is a weird day. The week isn't over, but you are. Mental Reset is one hour at the end of the workday where nobody needs anything from you. You come in, you lie down on a mat, you get a blanket and a bolster, and for the next sixty minutes your only job is to listen. I play crystal singing bowls, guide you through a short meditation so your mind has something to do besides replay the day, and offer Reiki while you rest. Most people tell me some version of the same thing afterward: the noise in their head finally turned down. Not off: down. Enough that they can go home and actually be home, instead of answering emails in their head at the dinner table. You don't need experience. You don't need to know how to meditate, and you definitely don't need to “clear your mind.” If you could do that, you wouldn't need this class. First-timers are in the room most weeks. There are ten spots. That's deliberate. It's a small room, I can see everyone in it, and it never feels like an event. It feels like an exhale. A few regulars started as skeptics; more than one of our Google reviews comes from someone who arrived doubting the whole thing and left surprised at how settled they felt. You don't have to believe in anything for an hour of sound and rest to do you some good. Run by Victoria Vita: CPA for 20+ years, healer for 7+. I sat behind a desk with a brain that wouldn't switch off for a long time before I found this work. Thursday nights are built for the person I used to be. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Come straight from work. Leave like the week let go of you first. events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: NextStop Theatre’s:  The Elaborate Entrance of Chad Deity
events.description: NextStop Theatre presents The Elaborate Entrance of Chad Deity from November 5th–29th, 2026, at 269 Sunset Park Drive in Herndon, Fairfax County, Virginia. This Pulitzer Prize-finalist comedy by Kristoffer Diaz body-slams the world of pro-wrestling, pop culture, and the performance of identity. Told through the eyes of Macedonio "The Mace" Guerra, a gifted wrestler stuck being paid to lose to a bigger-named star in the ring, this knockout satire takes on cultural stereotypes, media spectacle, and the courage it takes to say no. A bold, tour-de-force comedy that leaves it all on the mat! Directed by Stefan Sittig, a multi-disciplined theatre veteran with 140+ productions across New York City, international venues, and D.C.-area theaters, the production features Sittig's expertise as a Helen Hayes Award-nominated director, choreographer, and fight director. Kristoffer Diaz, the playwright and screenwriter, is also known for his musical Hell's Kitchen (created with Alicia Keys), nominated for 13 Tony Awards and currently running on Broadway. Audience advisories include strong language, simulated violence/fighting, racial stereotypes, and flashing lights and haze effects. The 2nd Sunday matinee will be a mask-required performance (masks provided). The Elaborate Entrance of Chad Deity combines theatrical excellence, sharp satire, and bold storytelling in Fairfax County, Virginia. Tickets are available through Ovationtix at https://ci.ovationtix.com/34310 . Box office: boxoffice@nextstoptheatre.org / (703) 481-5930x1. events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.description: SEIZED Film Screening & Discussion SEIZED is a gripping, stranger-than-fiction investigative film that plunges audiences inside the troubling police raid on the Marion County Record. What begins as a shocking small-town incident quickly spirals into a national story, exposing how corruption, politics, and decades-long tensions turned a quaint Kansas community into a battleground over the First and Fourth Amendments. Blending the juicy intrigue of a classic muckraking narrative with a clear-eyed exploration of power, politics, and the fragility of a free press, SEIZED transforms a headline-grabbing event into a deeply human story that is urgent, unsettling, and impossible to ignore. The screening will be followed by a discussion and Q&A featuring the film director, Sharon Liese, and others. events.title: Unfossilizing African Art
events.description: Presented after extensive research, this exhibition recontextualizes African material culture objects held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. Image: Once Known Mende carver [Mende, Sierra Leone], Sowei, 19th-20th century, wood, varnish, 16 H x 10 W x 10 D in. Gift of Stephen A. Spear, 1975 (P.75.2.30)

events.title: Visit Brandywine Museum of Art and N.C. Wyeth House & Studio – A Bus Tour with Historic Annapolis
events.description: Join Historic Annapolis for a delightful day trip to Brandywine Museum of Art! You’ll enjoy a guided tour of the Brandywine Museum of Art, followed by a visit to the historic N.C. Wyeth House & Studio. Discover a distinguished collection of nineteenth- and twentieth-century American art, housed in a renovated nineteenth-century mill with a dramatic steel and glass addition that overlooks the bucolic Brandywine River. In 1911, artist N.C. Wyeth used proceeds from his Treasure Island illustrations to buy 18 acres near Chadds Ford, Pennsylvania. Today, the preserved house and studio feature original props, a large mural, and period furnishings that offer a glimpse into Wyeth’s work and family life. The day also includes a delicious lunch and free time to stroll through the beautiful gardens, galleries or browse the museum gift shop. Reserve your seat today—space is limited! Advance registration required; space is limited. Recommended for ages 16+. Cost : $175 General Admission. $160 for HA Members, Volunteers, and Military. Registration is now closed! Please call or email Dana Connett for availability: 443-221-6969 or dana.connett@annapolis.org

events.title: A Gift in Motion
events.description: A multidisciplinary showcase from the artists and scholars of the full-time faculty and staff at the Corcoran School of the Arts & Design. A Gift In Motion loosely draws from Robin Wall Kimmerer’s book The Serviceberry which uplifts Indigenous frameworks of the natural world to advance the possibilities in collectivity, reciprocity, and the mindset of abundance. These are anti-capitalist models and theories that provide insight into the systems of power we negotiate, but also offer a lens on how we individually move through our daily lives—together—through historically fraught landscapes. A keen reminder that working with, for, and because of each other remains the most human motivation, even while we are inundated with narratives that suggest otherwise. Within the walls of the academy, frameworks of artistic and creative knowledge are often dismissed, as are Indigenous methodologies and community-focused perspectives that center human engagement, oral and craft-based practices, and unquantifiable research. A personal experience. A feeling. Abstraction. And yet, for centuries, within the walls of art schools exist myriad economies of imagination that are anchored in the sharing of diverse creative knowledge and articulated in what we make, write, perform, dance, build, conserve, collect, display, speak, and think. events.title: Annapolis Jazz & Roots Festival
events.description: Annapolis Jazz & Roots is launching its fifth festival on the scenic shores of the Chesapeake Bay. Events combine music, art, poetry and history on two weekends, November 6-15. Based in the maritime community of Eastport, the festival includes eight venues in nearby neighborhoods. Each has its own distinct character and charm. Festival goers can visit centuries old buildings, take in restorative bay views and stroll the tree-lined streets of the historic Maryland city. THEME AND HIGHLIGHTS The 2026 theme “New World Music: Centuries of Sound” will be brought home by international and regional performers. An adventurous lineup includes programs rooted in history and culture from colonial days to modern times. Trace the evolution of music and culture since the days Indigenous tribes walked the forests and rode the waters. Gain new insights into the startling history and legacy of slavery and indenture in Maryland; delve into the soulful roots of jazz, and celebrate the changing color of sound in America. Events are free or require modest admission, and all but two venues offer free onsite parking. Reservations are strongly advised for all events. Tickets are sold through instantseats.com. WEEKEND ONE Opening Night takes place Friday, November 6 at 7:00 p.m. at St. Luke’s Episcopal Church in Eastport. Jazz lovers will appreciate how the intimacy and beautiful acoustics of the venue elevate the listening experience when the Muneer Nasser Band performs. Trumpeter Muneer Nasser was exposed to great music by his father, jazz bassist Jamil Nasser. This concert pays homage to three legendary musicians born in 1926: John Coltrane, Miles Davis and Randy Weston. Their brave explorations led to seismic shifts in the sonic landscape and continue to resonate around the globe. On Saturday at 11:00 a.m. visit Eastport-Annapolis Neck Library to gain new insights into slavery and indenture in colonial times. events.title: Briston Maroney: Normal Heights Tour
events.description: After growing up in Tennessee and Florida, singer, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist Briston Maroney has established himself as one of indie rock’s most compelling voices. In 2018, Maroney released his debut EP Carnival, featuring the RIAA Platinum-certified single Freakin’ Out On The Interstate. His sophomore album, Ultrapure (2023), produced by GRAMMY® winner Daniel Tashian, showcased his raw and earnest exploration of human emotion. Following Ultrapure, Maroney embarked on an extensive world tour, selling out headline shows across North America and Europe while appearing at festivals including Lollapalooza, Osheaga, and All Things Go. In May 2025, he released his acclaimed third studio album, Jimmy, before hitting the road on the expansive Long Hair, Long Life co-headline tour with Peach Pit, his biggest run of shows to date. In 2026, Maroney teamed up with flipturn for a collaborative covers project, further showcasing his versatility as an artist. With new music on the horizon, Briston continues to evolve while building a passionate global fanbase and cementing his place as one of indie music’s most exciting artists.

events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.

events.title: Caroline, or Change the Musical
events.description: 8 performances | October 31 and November 6*, 7, 13, and 14 at 7:30pm | November 1, 8, and 15 at 2:00pm *Friday, November 6 will include ASL interpretation and free tickets for Montgomery County residents! Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

events.title: Carsie Blanton
events.description: Carsie Blanton Carsie Blanton is a songwriter with hooks, chutzpah, and revolutionary optimism. A radical folk artist in the tradition of Woody Guthrie, her infectious melodies and lyrical wit keep listeners rapt while she conjures spirits of vaudeville, campfire singalongs, and punk rock. Blanton and her road-tested band deploy humor, camaraderie, and considerable musical muscle to enroll each audience in a rare vision of hope and solidarity. In addition to writing and performing music, Carsie works as a political organizer and activist. In fall of 2025, she participated in the Global Sumud Flotilla, a direct action to bring humanitarian aid to Gaza by sailboat. In early October, after a month at sea, she was imprisoned in Israel for five days along with hundreds of her comrades. Soon after, Blanton released The Little Flame, a song of solidarity covered widely on social media during her detention. The Little Flame features background vocals from Irish band Ye Vagabonds and Carsie’s Palestinian/New Zealander prison-mate Rana Hamida, and appears on her latest album, The Red Album Vol II. events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. Image: Boris Ignatovich (Russian, 1899-1976), Composer Dmitri Shostakovich, from "Ignatovich, Soviet Avant-Garde", 1928, gelatin silver print, 16 H x 20 W in. events.title: Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY
events.description: For Freedoms presents artist and educator Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY which centers on Ethiopian journalist and author Baalu Girma’s controversial 1984 Amharic novel Oromay, written under the Derg regime and banned shortly after its publication. Drawing on Gottesman’s deep engagement with the novel, NIGHT AND DAY considers how artists create, communicate, and sustain cultural memory within and against conditions of censorship, political repression, and state violence. The exhibition extends beyond the gallery through a library of banned books, a self-guided workshop station that invites visitors to respond to censorship through writing and drawing, and a public conversation on how artists sustain creative practice amid sociopolitical pressure.

events.title: Forces of Nature with violinist Francesca Anderegg
events.venue: Maryland Hall for the Creative Arts
events.description: ANNAPOLIS SYMPHONY ORCHESTRA FORCES OF NATURE Friday, November 6, 2026 Saturday, November 7, 2026 6:30 PM Pre Concert Lecture 7:30 PM Concert At Maryland Hall MUSIC PROGRAM Luke Soneral An Overture: The Mouse and its Shadow Reinaldo Moya Vestido de Mar, with violinist Francesca Anderegg Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky The Tempest, Op. 18 Igor Stravinsky Divertimento from Le baiser de la fée (The Fairy’s Kiss) This concert is approximately 2 hours in length, with a 20 minute intermission. In Forces of Nature, the natural world becomes a source of wonder, reflection, and transformation. Emerging composer Luke Soneral opens the program with An Overture: The Mouse and Its Shadow, offering an exciting glimpse of orchestral music’s future. Reinaldo Moya’s ocean-inspired violin concerto, Vestido de Mar, brings violinist Francesca Anderegg to the stage for a work that reflects the landscapes and experiences of the Americas. Tchaikovsky’s The Tempest turns Shakespeare’s storm into a powerful exploration of human nature, while Stravinsky’s The Fairy’s Kiss honors Tchaikovsky through the wintry world of Hans Christian Andersen. Together, these works reveal nature as both an elemental force and a mirror of our inner lives.

At the fort, explore the earthworks that still stand today and imagine what life was like inside this military post. Rangers will share stories of daily routines, military strategy, and the experiences of those who served here. This hike offers a chance to experience history where it happened while connecting with the natural landscape that surrounds it. This program begins at the Rock Creek Park Nature Center.

events.title: From Consuming to Contributing: How We Built the Space That Was Missing
events.description: Hear from GW Engineering alumnus, Saquib Saifee, M.S. '23, at OWASP Global AppSec USA in San Fransciso, CA! On November 6, he, Caroline Lee, and Gaurang Deshpande from IBM will be leading the panel, "From Consuming to Contributing: How We Built the Space That Was Missing." Many of us naturally drift from consuming OWASP resources to contributing to them. At some point, you stop just reading the Top 10 and start showing up at a chapter, submitting a pull request, or volunteering at a conference. But what often gets lost is the "together" part. The shared strategy, the mutual encouragement, a place where experienced contributors can mentor others and people new to contributing can find their footing without having to figure it out alone. It started when two of us ran into each other at the Boston Application Security Conference. Same organization, same department, had no idea the other was there. That conversation grew into three people, then a cross-regional group, and eventually an initiative with executive sponsorship built around a simple question: what if there was a structured space where people at all levels of OWASP engagement could come together, share what they know, coordinate where to show up, and help each other go deeper? That is what we built. A space where seasoned contributors have a home for their work and a way to pass it on, and where people curious about OWASP but not sure where to start can learn, get mentored, and take their first real steps. Gaelic Storm, a multi-national, Celticjuggernaut grows stronger with each live performance, and after two decades and over 2000 shows, they are a true force to be reckoned with. The band attributes their continued success to their fanatic audience, and it’s a well-diversified crowd for sure – attracting fans of every genre with their richstorytelling, energetic instrumentals, devotion to Celtic traditions and passion for their stagecraft. They are as loyal to their fans as the fans are to them, as frontman Patrick Murphy states, “The fans are the ones that have given us this life. We’re here for them.” Gaelic Storm takes a true blue-collar, hard-nose approach to touring, consistently traveling the US and internationally forging a unique path in the Celtic musicworld. “You have to see us live. We are the true working-man’s’ band,” says longtime member Ryan Lacey. “We still, and most likely always will, tour most of theyear, and that’s how we constantly hone our craft.” This dedication to their live show dates all the way back to the mid-1990s, when Gaelic Storm kicked off its’ career as a pub band in Santa Monica, California. Onewhich performance led to their discovery that ultimately found the band appearing in the blockbuster film, Titanic (where they performed “Irish Party in ThirdClass”). This laid the groundwork for a career that would eventually find them topping the Billboard World Chart six times, making appearances at mainstreammusic festivals, and regularly headlining the largest Irish Festivals across the country, all while gaining a reputation as a genre-bending Irish rock band whosesongs mix Celtic traditions with something uniquely creative. Recent years have seen the addition of Natalya Kay on fiddle and Parker Hastings on guitar, who both bring their own energy, musicianship and spirit to GaelicStorm.

events.title: Gallery B Presents "Intersections | Realism & Abstraction"
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman - with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details. November 6, 2026 – November 29, 2026 Gallery Hours: Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, 12 – 5pm Opening Reception: Friday, November 6; 6 – 9pm

events.description: The Admissions Team is coming to Tysons on Friday, November 6, and we would love to sit down with you and your family. Pacific Preparatory is a Cognia-accredited online K-12 school. Every student learns through 1:1 live instruction that is built around that child, rather than asking the child to fit a school environment. Families can enroll full-time, add a single course, or work with our tutors for academic support, test prep, and enrichment. events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Rockville Musical Theatre presents “Caroline, or Change”
events.description: 8 performances | Oct. 31 and Nov. 6*, 7, 13 & 14 at 7:30 p.m. | Nov. 1, 8 & 15 at 2 p.m. Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving, and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four, working in a service job for a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child, but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. Caroline, or Change, produces a valuable theatrical experience that continues to thrill audiences the world over. It is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers for the better. Featuring one of the most powerful female roles in musi

events.description: Step into a more intentional approach to rest with a 75-minute, hands-on AcuAroma Therapy workshop that brings together the therapeutic traditions of essential oils and Traditional Chinese Medicine acupressure. Working with a carefully selected collection of high-quality organic essential oils, you’ll be introduced to three specific oil and acupressure point pairings chosen to support relaxation and restorative sleep. Your facilitator will explore the therapeutic qualities of each oil, the significance of the corresponding organ points, and, most importantly, how these points relate to and work together as part of a larger practice. This is both a learning experience and a moment of self-pampering. You’ll have time to slow down, work with the oils directly, and learn a simple ritual you can return to whenever your body and mind need help transitioning into deeper rest. You’ll also leave with your own take-home collection of therapeutic oils, along with a laminated reference card featuring images of the three acupressure points so you can confidently locate and practice them at home. The goal is not simply to experience the work in the room, but to give you the knowledge, tools, and quality ingredients to make it part of your own evening ritual. No prior experience is needed. Come as you are, and leave with a deeper understanding of how aromatic medicine and acupressure can be thoughtfully combined to support your wellbeing.

events.title: Short Course: An Overview of LLMs for Statisticians: Foundations, Reasoning and Agentic AI
events.description: The GW Department of Statistics presents, An Overview of LLMs for Statisticians: Foundations, Reasoning, and Agentic AI, a short course taught by Linjun Zhang, associate professor in the Department of Statistics and an affiliated faculty member in computer science at Rutgers University Date/Time: November 6, 2026 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Lunch break: 12:00–1:30 p.m. Description: This short course provides an overview of the foundations and frontiers of modern large language models (LLMs), with an emphasis on topics relevant to statisticians and data scientists. We will begin with the basic principles underlying embeddings, transformers, and the LLM training pipeline, including pretraining, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning from human feedback. Building on these foundations, we will discuss recent developments in reasoning models and agentic AI, including context engineering, harness engineering, and the design of AI agents for complex tasks. We will also discuss key issues in AI safety, reliability, and evaluation. The short course will combine conceptual foundations with practical examples and hands-on activities, with the goal of helping participants understand, use, and critically evaluate modern AI systems. Short Bio: Linjun Zhang is an Associate Professor in the Department of Statistics and an affiliated faculty member in Computer Science at Rutgers University. He received his Ph.D. in Statistics from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylva

events.title: Unfossilizing African Art
events.description: Presented after extensive research, this exhibition recontextualizes African material culture objects held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. Image: Once Known Mende carver [Mende, Sierra Leone], Sowei, 19th-20th century, wood, varnish, 16 H x 10 W x 10 D in. Gift of Stephen A. Spear, 1975 (P.75.2.30)

events.title: 250 Years of America
events.description: From the stirring opening call of Copland’s Fanfare for the Common Man to the irresistible exuberance of Sousa’s The Stars and Stripes Forever , this program travels through a distinctly American musical landscape. Along the way, you’ll hear the open-hearted simplicity and rhythmic vitality of Copland, the sweeping drama of Richard Rodgers’ Victory at Sea , the patriotic brilliance of Morton Gould’s American Salute , and the rich Romanticism of George Whitefield Chadwick’s Symphony No. 3. Arrive early for a special pre-concert performance by RCO’s principal strings featuring chamber music by Chadwick—a more intimate introduction to one of America’s important early orchestral voices. Bold, lyrical, nostalgic, and unmistakably American, this is a celebration 250 years in the making. Program Aaron Copland – Fanfare for the Common Man Aaron Copland – Hoedown, from the ballet, Rodeo Aaron Copland – Variations on a Shaker Melody, from Appalachian Spring Richard Rogers – Victory at Sea Morton Gould – American Salute George Chadwick – Symphony #3 John Phillip Sousa – Stars and Stripes Forever Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: A Gift in Motion
events.description: A multidisciplinary showcase from the artists and scholars of the full-time faculty and staff at the Corcoran School of the Arts & Design. A Gift In Motion loosely draws from Robin Wall Kimmerer’s book The Serviceberry which uplifts Indigenous frameworks of the natural world to advance the possibilities in collectivity, reciprocity, and the mindset of abundance. These are anti-capitalist models and theories that provide insight into the systems of power we negotiate, but also offer a lens on how we individually move through our daily lives—together—through historically fraught landscapes. A keen reminder that working with, for, and because of each other remains the most human motivation, even while we are inundated with narratives that suggest otherwise. Within the walls of the academy, frameworks of artistic and creative knowledge are often dismissed, as are Indigenous methodologies and community-focused perspectives that center human engagement, oral and craft-based practices, and unquantifiable research. A personal experience. A feeling. Abstraction. And yet, for centuries, within the walls of art schools exist myriad economies of imagination that are anchored in the sharing of diverse creative knowledge and articulated in what we make, write, perform, dance, build, conserve, collect, display, speak, and think. events.description: Join us for our monthly Open House featuring a special exhibit: Engines of Progress: Innovation and Trains . Discover how railways revolutionized travel and explore the clever problem-solving—including work by local inventors—that made the tracks safer and better. As an added feature, the Washington, Baltimore & Annapolis Chapter of the Train Collectors Association will have an operating layout in the Schoolhouse. Train Layout & Fun: Get an up-close look at this operating model train layout. Young engineers can put on an engineer's hat, sound the bell and whistle, and blow the horn! Plus, Final Bidding: Place your final bids on a vintage, fully furnished Magnuson "Queen Victoria" dollhouse. Designed by renowned model railroad pioneer Robert Lunde (of Lunde Studios and Magnuson Models), this 1:12 scale masterpiece features his iconic, handcrafted resin-cast brickwork and intricate traditional architecture. Bidding officially closes at 2 PM today! Can’t make it in person? You can view photos, watch a video tour, and place your online bid here: www.sydenstrickerschoolhouse.org/dollhouse/ All auction proceeds directly benefit our upcoming 100th birthday schoolhouse restoration work. Thank you for supporting local history!

Her massive talent has also been recognized at scale: her songs have been adapted for major performances with symphony orchestras, and she’s been tapped for prestigious tributes to Leonard Cohen and The Band. Since releasing her debut in 2007, she has shared a stage with artists including Arcade Fire, The National, Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds, Daniel Lanois, St Vincent, Sufjan Stevens, Destroyer and Andrew Bird. Bulat was born in Toronto and grew up listening to her mother’s piano students, Sam Cooke and Stax on the oldies station. In early 2016 she released, Good Advice, produced by Jim James of My Morning Jacket.

events.title: Brady Art Gallery Tour: Unfossilizing African Art and Cracks & Reforms
events.description: Take a student-led tour of the exhibitions currently on view at the Brady Art Gallery: "Unfossilizing African Art" and "Cracks and Reforms". Unfossilizing African Art recontextualizes African material culture objects that have been held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students across four seminar courses conducted original research to deepen understanding of the collection and reconsider how these objects are interpreted and exhibited. Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection examines a decade shaped by political upheaval, social transformation, migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition. This exhibition, developed as part of an art history class taught by Associate Professor Bibi Obler, is accompanied by a catalog designed by graphic design students.

events.title: Breathwork on the Farm
events.description: What: A regenerative morning of breathwork Where: The Studio at Honey’s Farmhouse (5819 Brooks Woods Road, Lothian MD 20711) When: Saturday November 7, 2026, 10am-12pm Instructor: Trish Brewer, Certified Breathwork Coach Release, reset, and restore through the breath. Join Certified Breathwork Coach Trish D. Brewer for a Breathwork Circle at the Studio at Honey's Farmhouse and discover how our breath offers us the regenerative power to restore what has been wounded or is inactive within us.⁣ Whether you are new to breathwork or have practiced many times, all welcome. Please read and sign Trish Brewer's Client Introduction & Informed Consent form before you purchase your ticket. About Breathwork: Active Breathwork is a technique that allows you to disconnect from the thinking mind and enter a different state of consciousness. This type of Breathwork can lessen anxiety, depression, and stress. It can release emotional or mental blocks, constriction, tension, trauma, fear, grief, and/or anger.⁣⁣ What to Bring: Yoga mat and/or blanket(s) Eye covering (a bandanna or scarf will do, something to block the light) A journal to write in after Water to sip on before and after Please Note: Breathwork can stir up deep emotions with the intention of lightening things up for you, but it can also be a lot to navigate. It is always my intention to create nurturing and compassionate space.⁣ Consult a doctor before participating in breathwork if you are pregnant, have been diagnosed with cardiovascular disease, suffer from high blood pressure, epilepsy, glaucoma, retinal detachment, aneurysms, osteoporosis, have had recent surgery, or physical injury, have a history of severe mental illness or panic attacks.⁣ Before you purchase, please read and sign Trish Brewer’s Client Introduction & Informed Consent form. This is required for all attendees before every Breathwork Circle. One ticket per attendee is required. Tickets are nonrefundable and nontransferable.

events.title: Camp One Heartland
events.description: Camp One Heartland is a solo exhibition by Tye DuSold-O’Connor archiving documentation of one of the world’s first nonprofit summer camps designated to supporting and empowering youth affected by HIV and AIDS, eventually transforming into a vital beacon of safety, liberation and eutopia for LGBTQ+ youth across the country. After its inaugural session in the summer of 1993 and many more held at different campsites across the country, Camp One Heartland found its permanent residence in Willow River, Minnesota. Over the next three decades it broadened its reach to provide summer camp sessions for youth experiencing housing instability, LGBTQ+ youth, and specifically trans youth. Tye attended Camp One Heartland as both a camper in 2022 and a counselor in 2024, and found these experiences indescribably transformative to them and their queer identity. Quite suddenly, Camp One Heartland shut down permanently in the fall of 2024 due to financial issues. Former campers, counselors and staff have been unable to return to the site since. While camp counseling in the summer of 2024, Tye took hundreds of photos of the camp, its people, and its experiences. These serve as some of the last images taken during the lifetime of Camp One Heartland. events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.
