events.description: 8 performances | October 31 and November 6*, 7, 13, and 14 at 7:30pm | November 1, 8, and 15 at 2:00pm *Friday, November 6 will include ASL interpretation and free tickets for Montgomery County residents! Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. events.title: Exhibition Openings: FOCUS at The Delaplaine
events.description: Exhibition Openings: FOCUS at The Delaplaine Saturday, November 7 • 3–5 pm FREE View exhibitions and meet the artists! These exhibitions are opening on Saturday, November 7 and can be viewed starting at 9 am. Beat the crowds and visit us earlier in the day! Nov 7–29 National Juried Photography Exhibition Part of FOCUS: A Celebration of Photography, the NJPE takes place every other year in November. The exhibition features selected photographs by regional and national artists. ABOUT THE JUROR: E. Brady Robinson is a Baltimore-based photographer and creative director known for her vibrant and eclectic mix of fine art photography, cultural documentation, and portraits of creatives. Her work has been featured in solo and group exhibitions in the US and internationally, and her photographs are held in the permanent collections of the Orlando Museum of Art and the Spanish Cultural Center in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. Robinson teaches photography and senior seminar at Georgetown University and is a contributing photographer for BmoreArt and Baltimore Beat. Nov 7–29 Mark Seaver Beauty Through Thin Ice Photography Seaver’s photography uses ice and its properties as a filter through which to photograph. The result is the refraction of light, which distorts and abstracts the world seen through it. Nov 7–29 Christophe Casamassima The Dirty Window Photography The Dirty Window is a phantasmagoric cycle of photography that aligns with the four stages of sleep. Casamassima uses photography to explore how repetition reveals difference and where latent images surface to consciousness before dissolving again. Nov 7–29 Kevin Stivers Elsewhere Photography Elsewhere exists between places, neither here nor there. The work in Stiver’s exhibition explores themes of human connection and disconnect and feelings of belonging and misplacement, shrouded in a surreal atmosphere.

events.title: FACETED Seminar Series | Hand Sculpted: The Art & Evolution of Engraving
events.description: Join the InBloom team on Saturday, November 7th at 3PM in their Downtown Frederick gallery for the next talk in the FACETED seminar series— Hand Sculpted: The Art & Evolution of Engraving . A hand-engraved line isn’t simply applied to jewelry—it deliberately transforms the metal. For centuries, engravers have cut controlled lines into metal to preserve names, create intricate patterns, and bring surfaces and stories to life through texture, light, and shadow. It’s a beautiful expression of InBloom Jewelry’ philosophy: artistry in service to love. Whether a meaningful date inside a band, a name rendered in script, or a hand-cut design inspired by a personal story, hand engraving makes jewelry deeply personal and enduring—meticulously carved by a person, for a person (or by the InBloom goldsmiths, for you). This seminar will include a fascinating discussion on the history and evolution of hand engraving and a live demonstration of this centuries-old art form. Free to all, RSVPs encouraged.

events.title: Forces of Nature
events.description: In Forces of Nature , the natural world becomes a source of wonder, reflection, and transformation. Emerging composer Luke Soneral opens the program with An Overture: The Mouse and Its Shadow , offering an exciting glimpse of orchestral music’s future. Claire Lewis will guest conduct. Reinaldo Moya’s ocean-inspired violin concerto, Vestida de mar (Clothed by the sea) , brings violinist Francesca Anderegg to the stage for a work that reflects the landscapes and experiences of the Americas. Tchaikovsky’s The Tempest turns Shakespeare’s storm into a powerful exploration of human nature, while Stravinsky’s The Fairy’s Kiss honors Tchaikovsky through the wintry world of Hans Christian Andersen. Together, these works reveal nature as both an elemental force and a reflection of our inner lives. events.title: From Grief to Becoming: A Guided Meditation for Identity Transitions with Danielle Kean Grassi
events.address: 30 W. Potomac St., Ste 102, Brunswick, MD 21716
events.description: Healing often brings an unexpected kind of grief. As you grow, you may notice yourself letting go of old roles, relationships, beliefs, or ways of coping that once helped you survive. While this transformation can be beautiful, it can also feel uncertain. This 90-minute guided meditation is a deeply reflective, primarily meditative experience designed to support you through that in-between space—not who you once were, but not yet fully who you're becoming. Through grounding practices, breath awareness, nervous system support, visualization, and gentle reflection, you'll be invited to notice what you're carrying, reconnect with your body's wisdom, and cultivate greater capacity for change with compassion. Because everyone's emotional experience is unique, participants are encouraged to move at their own pace. You're always welcome to pause, open your eyes, or simply observe if that feels most supportive. This offering is best suited for those navigating life transitions, personal growth, changing identities, or the emotional experience of becoming someone new. Feel free to bring along a journal and pen for reflection.

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

The premiere will take place on Saturday, November 7, 2026, with doors opening at 6:00 PM and the film beginning at 7:00 PM. Through themes of aging, gratitude, forgiveness, and reconnection, the film encourages viewers to pause, reflect, and honor the people who shaped their lives. Brought to life by director Bruce Odams and writer/producer/co-director Dr. Gybrilla Ballard Blakes, the film weaves heartfelt storytelling with real-world impact. Their collaboration creates a moving cinematic experience that resonates with families, caregivers, and communities everywhere.

events.address: 1801 Hawkins Road, Crownsville, MD, 21401, Crownsville, MD 21032
events.description: Protect the Health of YOUR Local Forest: Join us at Bacon Ridge Natural Area in Crownsville to spend a morning removing harmful invasive plants from along the trails! Scenic Rivers’ Healthy Forests Program engages community volunteers to help protect the long-term vitality of our largest conservation easement located within Bacon Ridge Natural Area. Our October 2026 workday will focus on vines, shrubs, and grasses. These aggressive invaders threaten vegetation at all levels of the forest from the ground up into the forest canopy. Event Details: Volunteers will be working on designated trail sections to remove specific invasive plant species. Volunteers will be trained in how to identify and remove these plants. Work gloves and tools can be provided by Scenic Rivers, though volunteers are welcome to bring their own gear. To participate, volunteers must: Be 16 years or older to attend without a supervising adult. Volunteers age 10 to 15 may attend with an accompanying adult(s) to supervise work; Be able to hike up to 1 mile to get to designated work areas. Wear long sleeve shirts, long pants, and closed toed shoes. Poison ivy is present in these work areas. Bring a full water bottle. We must have at least 5 registered volunteers for the workday to proceed. So, be sure to invite some friends! Controlling invasive species infestations is a big job and we’ll be happy to have as much help as possible!

events.title: Maryland Emancipation Day
events.address: 8000 Walker Mill Road, Capitol Heights, MD 20743
events.description: What We Carried into Freedom: Knowledge • Skill • Culture • Community Join us at Concord Historic Site for the Maryland Emancipation Day Celebration, an afternoon of living history, music, storytelling, food, family, and community as we commemorate the abolition of slavery in Maryland. Maryland’s Constitution of 1864 took effect on November 1, ending slavery in the state and freeing more than 30,000 African Americans. At Concord—a former tobacco plantation where generations of African Americans were enslaved—Emancipation Day offers an opportunity to remember that history while exploring what freedom made possible. Throughout the afternoon, discover the skills, knowledge, creativity, and cultural traditions African Americans carried through enslavement and used to build lives, families, businesses, institutions, and communities after emancipation. A Celebration Rooted in History Craft Demonstration Area Meet skilled artisans and tradition bearers demonstrating historic and contemporary crafts while discovering the knowledge, creativity, and craftsmanship behind their work. The Griot Sound Stage Experience the power of African American music, storytelling, spoken word, and performance. Inspired by the African tradition of the griot as a keeper of history and community memory, the stage brings stories of culture, freedom, and resilience to life. Hands-On History: Community Glass Project Leave your mark on Concord’s story. Participate in a special, hands-on glass activity connected to the artwork being created for the historic site and learn how community voices are becoming part of Concord’s evolving interpretation. Food Pavilion Take a break, gather around the table, and enjoy food available from participating vendors throughout the celebration.

Valerie Tripp, beloved writer of companion novels for characters like Felicity, Josefina, Samantha, Kit, Molly, Maryellen, and the WellieWishers™, will share her journey as a children’s author. Ms. Tripp will discuss her creative process, inspirations, and experiences bringing these iconic characters to life. The event will conclude with a Q&A session followed by a book signing. Please bring your own books; copies will not be available for purchase at the event. Advance registration recommended; space is limited. Cost: General Admission: $7. Free for HA members, Military, and children 17 and under. This event is also offered at 1 0:30AM. About our Presenter: Valerie Tripp (Yale ’73; Harvard GSE ’82) is the award-winning author of American Girl books, plays, and short stories about Felicity, Josefina, Samantha, Kit, Molly, and Maryellen as well as the Welliewisher and Hopscotch Hill School series. Tripp also wrote a STEM series for National Geographic Kids and is the executive editor of the Boys Camp series. She is has adapted classics for Sterling Publishers, and has written numerous leveled readers, songs, stories, nonfiction essays, skills book pages, poems, and plays for educational publishers. Tripp has spoken at The Smithsonian, The New York Historical Society, Mt. Vernon, The Daughters of the American Revolution Annual Luncheon, Yale University, Harvard Graduate School of Education, and The Library of Congress in addition to countless schools, libraries, writers’ groups, podcasts, book stores, scout troops, and organizations that encourage young women such as Girls on the Run and Yes, She Can. Accessibility: This program is fully accessible, including a flat accessible entryway and elevator access to restrooms. events.title: Montgomery County History Conference
events.description: The Montgomery County History Conference Returns November 7! Montgomery College’s Bioscience Education Center on the Germantown Campus This year’s History Conference will open with a keynote by author David O. Stewart, describing the daunting task that the drafters of the Constitution faced in the summer of 1787. Throughout the day, concurrent sessions will cover an interesting variety of topics such as Native American archaeology in Montgomery County, disability rights in Maryland, the history of the FDA, and many more. Anthony Cohen will close the session with reflections on his recent journey called “Freedom Walk 2026,” the 750-mile pilgrimage he took following 19th-century routes to freedom on the Underground Railroad to Canada. As always, your ticket purchase includes a boxed lunch and a catered reception. Join friends and fellow history enthusiasts on November 7 for the Montgomery County History Conference!

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: November First Saturday Open House at FBAC
events.description: Join us for our November First Saturday where three new exhibits will be opening in the Gallery focusing on civic engagement in the arts. Ellen Mansfield's "Deaf Line" explores the vibrant corridor of visual language, cultural resilience, and shared history. “Let Facts be Submitted to a Candid World” FBAC Altered Declaration Project, where artists in our community have taken a copy of the Declaration and altered it to express their thoughts and feelings about the current state of democracy in the United States. Corrine Wilson's community project featuring 12 signed "Protect Trans Kids" Eagle Flags will all be displayed in one place for the first time. 2pm - Talk by Peter Brehm on the nexus of art and the LGBTQ community. Followed by an artist talk from Ellen Mansfield on her show "Deaf Line" with an ASL interpreter. 4pm - Poetry reading by Tom Mande, Terence Winch, and Beth Joselow. 12-6pm - Print mini Declaration of Independence keepsakes on the Book Beetle with Josef Beery, creator of the Book Beetle! 12-6pm - Printing demo by Judith Kornett on our French Tool Press.

events.title: Now is Gone Book Signing & Author Event with Geoff Livingston - FREE
events.description: Now Is Gone: Think Liquid to Navigate Neverending Change Book Signing Change isn't coming. It's already here, and it isn't slowing down. AI is reshaping industries, eliminating roles, and rewriting the rules of business faster than any planning cycle can track. The old playbook, built on fixed strategies, binary thinking, and the illusion of control, no longer works. What got you here won't get you there. Now Is Gone offers a different path. Drawing on 30 years in AI consulting, technology marketing, and crisis communications, Geoff Livingston blends Buddhist philosophy with practical frameworks to help business professionals stop fighting change and start flowing with it. Copies of Geoff's book will be available and there will be time for book signings after his talk. He will also leave plenty of time for Q&A.

events.description: In this 60-minute, one-woman play, Denise Casey follows the river back through all the games she’s played to the source. From taking cover in a monastery to skip out of rehab to finding refuge in the trees until she could hear them speak and then time-traveling through a seventh-grade science class. Part memoir, part meditation, part make-believe, Playing the Game is unshaking in its exploration of imagination and courage. It will leave you singing, humming and remembering that another way is not only possible, but it’s on the way.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.description: 8 performances | Oct. 31 and Nov. 6*, 7, 13 & 14 at 7:30 p.m. | Nov. 1, 8 & 15 at 2 p.m. Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving, and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four, working in a service job for a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child, but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. Caroline, or Change, produces a valuable theatrical experience that continues to thrill audiences the world over. It is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers for the better. Featuring one of the most powerful female roles in musi

events.title: Saint Cecelia Harvest Wine Dinner and Ball
events.description: In the years before a national Thanksgiving Day friends and neighbors would gather for a harvest dinner, giving thanks for the blessings of the year and for the promise of the dawning of the next. These dinners always included social dancing such as the Virginia Reel. Because these celebrations occurred in November they became associated with Saint Cecelia, who in some liturgical calendars was identified as the patron of music. At Shiloh Manor Farm we continue this old Virginia tradition! We are partnering with Magnolias at the Mill to present a tradition Saint Cecelia dinner inspired by a 200 year old book on Virginia cooking authored by one of Patrick Henry’s granddaughters. Following dinner musicians from the Greater Washington Folklore Society will perform traditional English Country Dance tunes that were well known in colonial Virginia such as the Virginia Reel. Dan Gillespie, a highly respected historical dance master will be on hand to teach and call the dances. No experience needed! Comfortable clothing and shoes are a must but we encourage formal or historic attire. A prize will be awarded for best costume!

events.title: Silver Spring B&O Station Open House: The History of the Georgetown Branch of the B&O Railroad
events.venue: Silver Spring Baltimore and Ohio Railroad Station
events.description: Presentation on the Georgetown Branch at 12:30 (appropriate for ages 11 and up): The 11.5 mile branch stretched from just west of Silver Spring, MD across Rock Creek, through Chevy Chase and Bethesda, and along the palisades of the Potomac river into Georgetown in DC. Trains operated from 1892 until 1985 and the line featured a long, tall trestle, a tunnel, and industrial street running. Industries served included cement plants, lumber yards, fuel dealers, three power plants and even a Frito factory. Ben Sullivan will share the colorful history of the line through rare photographs, historic maps, and key stories from its 93-year run. Ongoing Activities: Enjoy train spotting and waving at the engineers, a model layout, a toy train play set, and photos and memorabilia of the railroad’s glory days and historic Silver Spring, plus show off your favorite train-related outfit!

events.description: Join Frederick home bakers Jon & Emily for a sourdough bread baking class designed for beginner bakers! Slow-fermented sourdough bread is beloved for its digestibility (especially for those of us with gluten sensitivity), lower glycemic index, and its keeping power without preservatives. Its complex, delicious flavor and airy, chewy texture cannot be beat! Beyond the joys of eating sourdough bread, many also enjoy the therapeutic nature of a slow, mindful hobby that doubles as a satisfying creative outlet. It's a science experiment you get to eat! In this 2-hour class, we will practice mixing, shaping, and baking a traditional sourdough bâtard (an oval-shaped loaf). You will leave class with: • your own sourdough starter (+ feeding instructions) • banneton proofing basket + cloth liner + bench scraper • a shaped dough to bake at home the same afternoon as class • a bonus dough to practice another shape & bake at home • printed and PDF versions of the recipe and instructions taught in class • support from your new sourdough bread baking friends!

Call 410-715-9596) The Central Maryland Chapter of the National Federation of the Blind of Maryland cordially invites you to examine the many technologies to help you read it your way. events.title: Unfossilizing African Art
events.description: Presented after extensive research, this exhibition recontextualizes African material culture objects held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. events.title: Walk in the Woods: Let’s be Smart About Winter Salt ft. Springsong Museum
events.description: Walk with us to discover the impact of winter salt to our waterways & learn more about the Springsong (Rachel Carson) Museum project. Step into the shoes of an environmental detective as we explore the hidden impacts of oversalting our streets and sidewalks during the winter season. Discover how excess salt harms delicate aquatic creatures, disrupts the fragile balance of our ecosystems, and pollutes our drinking water, and learn from the experts about what we can all do to be “winter salt smart.” The walk will also highlight the life and teachings of Silver Spring resident and writer/biologist Rachel Carson (1907-1964), with staff from Springsong Museum on hand to provide rich historical information and examples of Carson’s influential writings. Currently in development, Springsong Museum will transform the vacant building at Burnt Mills East Park into a community museum that connects the public and nature through the wonder and wisdom of Rachel Carson. Join the Izaak Walton League of America on this fun and informative hike to learn about our addiction to deicing salt and how we can all live on a low winter salt diet. Together, we can make a significant difference and create a cleaner, healthier future. Expect to walk a one mile loop on a dirt trail with a bit of rock scrambling at the end. Please bring your own water bottle. This event is FREE but please register on Eventbrite in case of delays or rescheduling due to bad weather. The rain date is Sunday, November 8. Izaak

events.title: Weekend Unwind: Sound Bath + Reiki : Saturday Mornings in Falls Church
events.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
events.description: Most people start their Saturday with a list. Groceries, errands, the thing they didn't finish on Friday, still buzzing around in their head. By the time they've “relaxed,” it's Sunday night. Weekend Unwind flips that. Eleven o'clock, one hour, lying down. Crystal singing bowls, a short guided meditation, and Reiki, in a small room with ten people in it and no agenda at all. Nothing to achieve, nothing to be good at. You just lie there and let the week drain out of your shoulders. This class has a different feel from our Thursday night one. Thursday is about switching off. Saturday is slower. People arrive less wound up, settle in faster, and tend to float out rather than rush out. Several regulars come as their standing Saturday thing, the way other people have a standing brunch. It pairs well with brunch afterwards, for the record. If you've never been to a sound bath: you keep your clothes on, you lie on a mat under a blanket, you close your eyes, and I do the rest. The bowls are played around and near you, the sound is physical as much as it is musical, you feel it in your chest, and an hour passes faster than you expect. Everything is provided. Show up in something comfortable with ten minutes to spare, and that's the whole preparation. I'm Victoria Vita. I've been a CPA for over twenty years and a healer for more than seven, and I teach every one of these classes myself. When you come back, and most people do, it's the same room, the same bowls, and the same person. That sameness is kind of the point. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Guests mention the warm welcome, feeling comfortable from the first visit, and booking again — that's the Saturday I try to run. What's included: • 60 minutes of crystal singing bowls, guided meditation and Reiki • Mat, blanket and bolster provided... just bring yourself • Ten spots only, so the room stays quiet and unhurried • A slow finish... no one is hustled out the door at noon Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: Award-winning DMV songstresses at Mackenzies this Sunday afternoon
events.description: Kipyn (Kai) Martin, Eryn Michel, and Rebecca Berlin join forces for a matinee of acoustic tunes this coming Sunday November 8th at Mackenzies in Old Town Fairfax. Tunes start at 4:00 pm and there is free parking nearby. Eryn Michel Eryn Michel’s songwriting walks the tightrope between real-life mess and wild imaginings—like her life, you’ll never be quite sure whether the Maryland mom and Army Veteran is singing truth, fiction, or a generous splash of both, drawn from a résumé that almost sounds made up: janitor, wedding planner, rifle instructor, Obama White House secret keeper, phlebotomist, voice actor, and private security for a king’s granddaughter. Her songs have earned her the 2024 Bernard/Ebb Songwriting Grand Prize, two American Songwriter lyric contest wins, and one First Place win for Modern Country in the Wide Open Country Song Contest . Maryland songwriter Eryn Michel has been writing folk, Americana, and country songs since the late nineteen hundreds, when she was raised in Los Angeles against her will. She shocked everyone who knew her when she enlisted in the Army not long after 9/11. Everywhere the Army sent her, a cheap guitar came too, so she could leave it with whoever was inspired to learn. After serving as a Civil Affairs sergeant and convoy gunner in Iraq, Eryn earned a bachelor’s degree in political science from UCLA, and then worked in the Obama White House. She finally soured on war and politics, and turned to music and motherhood to restore her soul

events.title: Canopy of Discovery
events.description: Experiencing history through outdoor mindfulness at Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House. About the Session: The sessions are approximately 90-minutes long and are conducted in relative silence. They include warm-ups, centering, and breathing exercises to connect participants to their bodies and the world around them. These are followed by a walk and an extended sit, which encourages participants to become more fully open and present to their surroundings. We conclude with a returning ritual and a chance to reflect on the experience. This time in nature will not be strenuous; most abilities can be accommodated. All ages are welcome, but children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult. Important Arrival & Check-In Details Check-In Location: All participants must check in at Woodlawn, regardless of session topic. Timing: Sessions start promptly at 12:00 PM (Sundays). events.title: Caroline, or Change the Musical
events.description: 8 performances | October 31 and November 6*, 7, 13, and 14 at 7:30pm | November 1, 8, and 15 at 2:00pm *Friday, November 6 will include ASL interpretation and free tickets for Montgomery County residents! Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

events.title: Cinema Art Bethesda: How to Divorce During the War
events.description: As part of its monthly film screening series, Cinema Art Bethesda is pleased to present Andrius Blaževičius’s award-winning 2026 film. Vilnius, Lithuania, 2022. High-flying executive Marija chooses the worst possible moment to inform her husband Vytas she wants a divorce: just one day before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Suddenly, the couple must navigate the process of separation in tandem with a refugee crisis as well as a mid-life crisis. A struggling film director, Vytas is forced to move in with his Russophile parents, while Marija sees the war impacting both her business and her home life. As the reason for the divorce becomes clear, the dissolution of Marija’s and Vytas’ marriage creates conflicts and opportunities for both of them while also affecting their ever-observant young daughter Dovile. Packed with surprises, Blaževičius’s family drama depicts the fallout of a marriage against the backdrop of extraordinary events with humor and compassion. events.title: Franni Cash: Here I Am Tour 2026
events.description: For fans of We The Kingdom, Jamie MacDonald, and CAIN Franni Cash doesn’t just say what’s on her mind; she sings it as loudly as possible. The GRAMMY® Award-nominated Platinum singer, songwriter, and producer isn’t afraid to speak truth to power, tear down false idols, or point out hypocrisy when it comes to religion, church, or “Country Club Christians” —as she does on the likes of “Church Clothes” and “Koolaid. ” Opening up about her doubts, questions, and struggles in conversation, at shows, and on tape has made her faith stronger and given her music meaning. To paint a personal picture, she chooses to sonically color outside of the lines. The songstress spikes soulful-style hooks with rock ‘n’ roll attitude, bringing soul to Americana-style instrumentation, as she laces a sly sense of humor into the fabric of her unapologetic storytelling. She even co-opts and reclaims words and phrases once used to lambast her (such as “Jezebel”) for her own. Now, Franni declares who she is on her 2026 debut LP , Here I Am. She intentionally arranged and sequenced this 13-track body of work to tell her story in the order that she wanted to. Over the course of the journey, she looked back on how far she’s come. “I don’t know anybody who hasn’t had a problem with religion at some point, ” she observes. “Just because you’ve been burned by a church or by broken people in the church, it doesn’t mean you can’t have faith. To me, that’s what this record is about. It’s about coming back to music and true faith in a relationship with God, addressing the pain and ultimately seeking to heal from it. ” Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.description: What: Local authors' book launch and signing Where: The Barn at Honey's Harvest Farm (5801 Brooks Woods Road, Lothian MD 20711) When: Sunday November 8, 2026, 12pm-4pm Join author, speaker, and Chesapeake Bay advocate Mick Blackistone along with well-known award-winning artist Mitzi Bernard at Honey's Harvest Farm as they celebrate the launch of their book, Women Who Work the Waters of the Chesapeake Bay . "I wrote this book with Mitzi Bernard about the women who work the waters of the Chesapeake and her tributaries because, in my opinion, it was past due. Mitzi and I fell 'in love' with each and every one of them because of their persistence, determination, dedication and deep abiding love for working as watermen. They are young and old. Married and single. They wouldn’t stand out in a crowd unless you see them for who they are: Hunter Gatherers in the deepest sense. They live for family, community, and commercial fishing. They work as hard as any man and they sweat as much too. Their sisters in Virginia can verify all of this as they, too, live the life from sunup to sundown." – Mick Blackistone SCHEDULE 12 noon - Meet the authors and purchase your autographed and signed book 1pm - Author presentation featuring the women who work the Chesapeake Bay 2pm-4pm - Authors available for book signing Copies of the book will be available to buy. events.title: Monocacy Battlefield Tour
events.description: The Battle that Saved Washington Battlefields have a remarkable habit of looking peaceful. You’d never guess they were once full of people making spectacularly bad days for one another. On July 9, 1864, Monocacy National Battlefield became the setting for the battle remembered as the “Battle That Saved Washington.” By delaying the Confederate advance on the nation’s capital, the Union forces bought precious time for Washington’s defenses, making Monocacy one of the Civil War’s most significant, and perhaps most underestimated, battlefields. Beginning at the Monocacy Battlefield Visitor Center , we’ll journey through the battlefield with a National Park Service guide who brings the battlefield to life., following the course of the fighting while uncovering the stories of the soldiers who fought here and the families whose homes suddenly found themselves in the middle of history. With an expert guide bringing the landscape to life, you’ll discover how a quiet stretch of Maryland came to play an extraordinary role in the nation’s story. History happened here in a single day. The consequences took rather longer. DURATION: 1 hour DEPARTS FROM: Monocacy National Battlefield, 5201 Urbana Pike Frederick, MD 21704 TICKETING DETAILS: $35 per person. A minimum total of 15 tickets must be sold for the tour to run. If we don’t sell the required minimum of tickets, we’ll gladly refund your purchase or credit it toward another exciting tour. We’re committed to ensuring you have a fantastic experience, and we appreciate your understanding as we work to create fun, unforgettable events together!

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.description: A series of immersive outdoor mindfulness sessions designed to help you slow down, cultivate curiosity, and deepen your connection to nature and history. They include warm-ups, centering, and breathing exercises to connect participants to their bodies and the world around them. These are followed by a walk and an extended sit which encourages participants to become more fully open and present to their surroundings. In a moment beset with polarization and misinformation, Maddows voice shines in this blistering demand to do better to rebuild the republic, and stronger this time. Rachel Maddow is the Emmy Award and Murrow Award winning host of The Rachel Maddow Show on MS NOW, as well as the New York Times bestselling author of Drift, Blowout, and Prequel, and the New York Times bestselling coauthor of Bag Man. Maddow received a bachelors degree in public policy from Stanford University and earned her doctorate in political science at Oxford University. She lives in New York City and Massachusetts with her partner, artist Susan Mikula. There is an overall 2 ticket limit for this event.

events.title: Rockville Musical Theatre presents “Caroline, or Change”
events.description: 8 performances | Oct. 31 and Nov. 6*, 7, 13 & 14 at 7:30 p.m. | Nov. 1, 8 & 15 at 2 p.m. Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving, and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four, working in a service job for a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child, but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. Caroline, or Change, produces a valuable theatrical experience that continues to thrill audiences the world over. It is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers for the better. Featuring one of the most powerful female roles in musi

events.title: "Inside Gaza" Film Screening & Discussion
events.description: The Institute for Middle East Studies is proud to announce a screening of the award winning documentary Inside Gaza, followed by remarks from film director Hélène Lam Trong and featured journalist Mai Yaghi. Since the Hamas attack on 7 October 2023 and the Israeli reprisals that followed, international journalists and media have no access to the Gaza Strip. Agence France-Presse journalists, who were permanently stationed in Gaza, were among the last independent witnesses to the abuses committed in the hellscape that Gaza has become. Featuring previously unseen footage and testimony from reporters Mai Yaghi and Adel Zaanoun, as well as photojournalists Mahmud Hams and Mohammed Abed, Inside Gaza delivers a powerful account of conditions on the ground, underscoring the vital importance of a free and independent press. All are invited to join the Institute for Middle East Studies for this film screening and discussion with film director Hélène Lam Trong and featured journalist Mai Yaghi. A trailer for the documentary can be found here. Speakers: Hélène Lam Trong is a French documentary filmmaker. Her 2023 documentary Daech, les enfants fantômes (ISIS, the Ghost Children) earned her the Albert Londres Prize for an audio-visual work. Independent since 2018, she worked for several years at Radio France then at France télévisions. In 2024, she directed Raqqa, l'ombre de Daech. events.title: Beyond Discovery: Archaeology, Heritage and Partnership in the Galilee
events.description: Join the CCAS Department of Classical and Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations for a presentation on the U.S.-funded Galilee Heritage Project at Huqoq and Bethsaida. Focusing primarily on Huqoq, this lecture traces the journey from archaeological discovery to conservation, interpretation and public engagement, including new finds from 2026, the Secrets of Huqoq exhibition and new digital initiatives. Speaker: Dr. Shua Kisilevitz, Albright Institute of Archaeological Research and Tel Aviv University About the Project: What happens to an archaeological site after excavation ends, but long before it can open to the public? The Galilee Heritage Project addresses this challenge at two recently excavated sites near the Sea of Galilee, the late Roman synagogue and extraordinary mosaics of Huqoq and the Byzantine church at Bethsaida (El-Araj), identified by its excavators as the Church of the Apostles. Together, these exceptional discoveries offer compelling windows into the culturally and religiously diverse world of the Galilee in Late Antiquity. Led by the W. F. Albright Institute of Archaeological Research with U.S. federal support, the project also highlights the enduring role of American scholarship and American-Israeli institutional partnership in researching, preserving and sharing the region's archaeological heritage.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Rick Steves
events.description: In the 1970s, the ultimate trip for any backpacker was the storied “Hippie Trail,” a 3,000-mile trek from Istanbul to Kathmandu. A 23-year-old Rick Steves made the trek in 1978, and like a travel writer in training, he documented everything along the way: jumping off a moving train, making friends in Tehran, getting lost in Lahore, getting high for the first time in Herat, battling leeches in Pokhara, and more. The experience ignited his love of travel and forever broadened his perspective on the world. On the Hippie Trail: Istanbul to Kathmandu and the Making of a Travel Writer —a New York Times bestseller now out in paperback—contains edited selections from Rick Steves’ journal and travel photos with a 45-years-later preface and postscript reflecting on how his journey through Turkey, Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, and Nepal changed his life.

events.title: A Virtual Lecture from Historic Annapolis – William and Dinah Nuthead: Maryland’s First Printers
events.description: Before Jonas and Anne Catharine Hoof Green, there was William and Dinah Nuthead, Maryland’s first printing duo. William Nuthead was the first printer in Maryland and the first to operate a press in Virginia, establishing his business in St. Mary’s City in 1685 after being barred from printing in Virginia by the colonial government. Following his death in 1695, his widow Dinah Nuthead took over the business and became the first licensed female printer in the American colonies. Join Rod Cofield as he discusses his research into their lives that led to his Maryland Historical Magazine article, “Much Ado about Nuthead.” The Historic Annapolis Virtual Lecture Series is offered free of charge thanks to the generosity of an anonymous donor. If you enjoy this program, we hope you will consider becoming a member or making a donation today to support Historic Annapolis and our mission to connect all people with our shared history. Can’t watch live? All lectures will be recorded. Please register and you’ll receive the link to watch the recording after the event. Advance registration required; registration closes on half-hour prior to lecture. Cost: FREE This lecture will be offered virtually by Zoom. Upon registration, you will be sent the link for the video conference to join on the evening of the lecture. If you do not receive your confirmation email after you register, please check your Spam folder, or email Cara Garside at cara.garside@annapolis.org . To learn more about Zoom and to download the app to your computer, visit the Zoom website . About Our Presenter: Rod Cofield is the Executive Director at Jefferson Patterson Park and Museum in Calvert County. He was previously the Executive Director at Historic London Town and Gardens in Edgewater, Maryland. Rod’s first museum job was at Historic St. Mary’s City where he learned how to use a colonial-era printing press. events.description: ABT Studio Company, the junior company of American Ballet Theatre, features rising stars of the ballet world between the ages of 16 and 21. ABT Studio Company prepares these outstanding young dancers, who hail from all over the globe, to enter American Ballet Theatre or other leading ballet companies worldwide. Nearly 85% of current dancers in American Ballet Theatre are alumni of ABT Studio Company, including most Soloists and Principal Dancers. The highly mobile ABT Studio Company serves as an ambassador for American Ballet Theatre by touring to venues large and small. In recent years, ABT Studio Company has performed in such international destinations as the United Kingdom, Greece, South Korea, the Philippines, Hong Kong, and Mexico and at a wide variety of US performing arts centers, universities, festivals, and galas. ABT Studio Company dancers perform favorite excerpts from the classical and neoclassical canons alongside inventive contemporary pieces, commissioning today’s brightest choreographers to create new ballets on the dancers each season. Performances feature a wide variety of styles, offering something for everyone to enjoy—from ballet newcomers to lifelong fans!

events.description: Join us for our upcoming Bioethics Interest Group Forum Hybrid Meeting to discuss Undocumented Populations and Access to Healthcare Access to healthcare remains a significant challenge for many undocumented individuals, raising important ethical questions about justice, human dignity, and the responsibilities of healthcare systems. Barriers related to insurance coverage, immigration status, fear of enforcement, and social determinants of health can limit access to essential medical services and contribute to health disparities. This webinar will explore the ethical, legal, and public health considerations surrounding healthcare access for undocumented populations, examining how healthcare providers, policymakers, and communities can balance competing priorities while promoting equitable and compassionate care. Join us for a thoughtful discussion on one of the most pressing healthcare access issues of our time. REGISTER HERE. events.title: LEE EMI (Emilee Petersmark of The Crane Wives)
Life of Courage: Bruce McCandless and the Pacific War
events.venue: U.S. Naval Institute's Jack C. Taylor Conference Center
events.description: Join the U.S. Naval Institute on 10 November 2026 at 10:30 AM ET at the Jack C. Taylor Conference Center, in Annapolis, MD for a look inside the new book Iron and Fire: The Pacific War Story of Destroyer Captain Bruce McCandless with Bruce McCandless III as he recounts his grandfather’s—Admiral Bruce McCandless—wartime experiences across the Pacific. Lieutenant Bruce McCandless was at Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941, fought aboard the heavy cruiser USS San Francisco (CA 38) through the brutal Guadalcanal campaign. Later promoted to captain, he commanded the destroyer USS Gregory (DD 802) during the final drive across the Pacific. Late in life, retiring as an admiral, he dictated his wartime memories to his daughter Sue; the manuscript was then set aside for many years. Iron and Fire draws on family letters, photographs, shipmates’ recollections, and stories passed down through generations to share his story. Registration and other Information: All in-person guests must register by 25 September 2026. Due to the requirements of the U.S. Naval Academy and the timing of this event, in person attendance is only open to U.S. citizens. The conference will take place at the U.S. Naval Institute's Jack C. Taylor Conference Center, which is located on the grounds of the U.S. Naval Academy. A limited amount of parking is available at the Jack C. Taylor Conference Center. We welcome our audience in-person and via live-stream on the U.S. Naval Institute’s YouTube Channel.

events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. events.title: Ted Scheinman for Jolt: My Electric Journey Out of Darkness
events.description: Growing up in a hyper-educated, artistic, eccentric family, Ted Scheinman, the son of a medical doctor and an English professor, spent much of his precocious childhood as a writer and performer—and his greatest performance was as someone who was happy. He recognized his depression early and recorded its effects in a series of tragicomic journals, always hoping that the ritual of doing so would palliate if not cure. While the clouds occasionally parted, particularly during Ted’s years of intellectual questing at Hotchkiss and Yale—and, fleetingly, through his emergence as a successful journalist—his gloom kept returning, seemingly more debilitating each time. Eventually, a series of emotional plunges deposited Ted, at age thirty-five, in a psych ward in Washington, DC. There, he began an intensive course of electroconvulsive therapy—considered by most a treatment of last resort. The controversial procedure saved his life, but it also exacted a price: he was now missing important pieces of his memory. By turns deeply gripping, startlingly perceptive, understatedly hilarious, and heartbreakingly poignant, particularly in Ted’s depiction of his romantic relationships, Jolt asks: How do our families shape who we are, for good and ill? How much of our character is ingrained versus sculpted by circumstances? How can we adapt when our memory fails? Perhaps most critically: What are we willing to sacrifice to have a chance at life? events.title: TRIVIUM: CROWN IN THE GRAVE WORLD TOUR
Virtual Lecture – William and Dinah Nuthead: Maryland’s First Printers
events.description: Before Jonas and Anne Catharine Hoof Green, there was William and Dinah Nuthead, Maryland’s first printing duo. William Nuthead was the first printer in Maryland and the first to operate a press in Virginia, establishing his business in St. Mary’s City in 1685 after being barred from printing in Virginia by the colonial government. Following his death in 1695, his widow Dinah Nuthead took over the business and became the first licensed female printer in the American colonies. Join Rod Cofield as he discusses his research into their lives that led to his Maryland Historical Magazine article, “Much Ado about Nuthead.” The Historic Annapolis Virtual Lecture Series is offered free of charge thanks to the generosity of an anonymous donor. If you enjoy this program, we hope you will consider becoming a member or making a donation today to support Historic Annapolis and our mission to connect all people with our shared history. Can’t watch live? All lectures will be recorded. Please register and you’ll receive the link to watch the recording after the event. Advance registration required; registration closes on half-hour prior to lecture. Cost: FREE

events.title: A Gift in Motion
events.description: A multidisciplinary showcase from the artists and scholars of the full-time faculty and staff at the Corcoran School of the Arts & Design. A Gift In Motion loosely draws from Robin Wall Kimmerer’s book The Serviceberry which uplifts Indigenous frameworks of the natural world to advance the possibilities in collectivity, reciprocity, and the mindset of abundance. These are anti-capitalist models and theories that provide insight into the systems of power we negotiate, but also offer a lens on how we individually move through our daily lives—together—through historically fraught landscapes. A keen reminder that working with, for, and because of each other remains the most human motivation, even while we are inundated with narratives that suggest otherwise. Within the walls of the academy, frameworks of artistic and creative knowledge are often dismissed, as are Indigenous methodologies and community-focused perspectives that center human engagement, oral and craft-based practices, and unquantifiable research. A personal experience. A feeling. Abstraction. And yet, for centuries, within the walls of art schools exist myriad economies of imagination that are anchored in the sharing of diverse creative knowledge and articulated in what we make, write, perform, dance, build, conserve, collect, display, speak, and think. events.title: Camp One Heartland
events.description: Camp One Heartland is a solo exhibition by Tye DuSold-O’Connor archiving documentation of one of the world’s first nonprofit summer camps designated to supporting and empowering youth affected by HIV and AIDS, eventually transforming into a vital beacon of safety, liberation and eutopia for LGBTQ+ youth across the country. After its inaugural session in the summer of 1993 and many more held at different campsites across the country, Camp One Heartland found its permanent residence in Willow River, Minnesota. Over the next three decades it broadened its reach to provide summer camp sessions for youth experiencing housing instability, LGBTQ+ youth, and specifically trans youth. Tye attended Camp One Heartland as both a camper in 2022 and a counselor in 2024, and found these experiences indescribably transformative to them and their queer identity. Quite suddenly, Camp One Heartland shut down permanently in the fall of 2024 due to financial issues. Former campers, counselors and staff have been unable to return to the site since. While camp counseling in the summer of 2024, Tye took hundreds of photos of the camp, its people, and its experiences. These serve as some of the last images taken during the lifetime of Camp One Heartland. events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.

events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. events.description: For Freedoms presents artist and educator Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY which centers on Ethiopian journalist and author Baalu Girma’s controversial 1984 Amharic novel Oromay, written under the Derg regime and banned shortly after its publication. Drawing on Gottesman’s deep engagement with the novel, NIGHT AND DAY considers how artists create, communicate, and sustain cultural memory within and against conditions of censorship, political repression, and state violence. events.title: LeVar Burton
events.description: Tracing the different eras of his life—from “Roots” to “Star Trek: The Next Generation” to “Reading Rainbow” and far beyond the camera—actor LeVar Burton fearlessly opens up about growing up during the Civil Rights Movement, being raised by a remarkable mother, and discovering his calling as a storyteller in Take My Word for It. He explores how acting has served as both a source of transformation and an escape from the most difficult parts of his past, while also confronting the challenges of being a parent, husband, and householder. As Burton honors the loved ones whose strength and resilience shaped him, he also asks what we owe to our ancestors and to each other, reflecting on the deep necessity he’s always felt to advocate for liberation and equity. Burton will be in conversation with Michele Norris, a Peabody and Emmy Award-winning journalist, the host of the podcast “ Your Mama’s Kitchen,” and the author of Our Hidden Conversations: What Americans Really Think About Race and Identity.

events.title: The Civil War
events.description: From 1861 to 1865, Americans fought each other with a ferocity unseen in the country’s history. The immediate cause of the war was the secession of the Southern states. However, the roots lay in growing tensions over slavery. By the time the last shots were fired, as many as 750,000 Americans had been killed, and four million enslaved people were freed. This traveling banner exhibition, from the Gilder Lehrman Institute of American History, examines the impact of the Civil War on Americans throughout the fractured nation. The exhibit will be on display at the Fairfax Museum and Visitor Center (10209 Main St.) from November 11 - December 4. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.description: THE SECRETS OF EASTER ISLAND FINALLY REVEALED! GET TICKETS Presented by: Picnic Theatre Company Directed and Written by Steve Rochlin On Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday, November 11, 12, and 13, join the Picnic Theatre Company at Dupont Underground for an epic adventure across time, The Secrets of Easter Island Finally Revealed! Easter Island and its awe-inspiring giant stone idols overlooking the Pacific Ocean have become the stuff of lore, along with Stonehenge and other marvels whose origins defy easy explanation. Mystery shows like Ancient Aliens and In Search Of have trafficked in supernatural theories of extra-terrestrial intervention, inter-dimensional beings, lost civilizations, and others. Based on a true story, The Secrets of Easter Island, Finally Revealed! takes a provocative, humorous journey across centuries to discover the truth about Easter Island. Along the way, we meet intrepid explorers, ambitious entrepreneurs, investigative journalists, brilliant scholars, and obsessive truth seekers who will stop at nothing to find answers. events.title: Unfossilizing African Art
events.description: Presented after extensive research, this exhibition recontextualizes African material culture objects held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. Image: Once Known Mende carver [Mende, Sierra Leone], Sowei, 19th-20th century, wood, varnish, 16 H x 10 W x 10 D in. Gift of Stephen A. Spear, 1975 (P.75.2.30)

events.description: Fathom Gallery Prospect Street (3251 Prospect Street NW, Suite 275) opens its doors on Wednesday, November 4 from 5PM to 7PM for an exhibit open house featuring Gathering Light, the first solo show by California artist Jennifer Magee. Guests are invited to enjoy light bites from Plan It to the T catering and bubbly while exploring the exhibit. Here, in Jennifer’s own words, is what inspired Gathering Light: “I have spent decades paying attention to the ordinary: a familiar path, a corner of the garden, the hour when light lands on a surface and stays just long enough to be noticed. My work is an argument for staying. In paint, cyanotype, and mixed media, I capture what daily attention gives back, with feeling always coming first. events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape. Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available. Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape.Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available.Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Experiencing history through outdoor mindfulness at Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House. About the Session: The sessions are approximately 90-minutes long and are conducted in relative silence. They include warm-ups, centering, and breathing exercises to connect participants to their bodies and the world around them. These are followed by a walk and an extended sit which encourages participants to become more fully open and present to their surroundings. We conclude with a returning ritual and a chance to reflect on the experience. This time in nature will not be strenuous; most abilities can be accommodated. All ages are welcomed but children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult. Important Arrival & Check-In Details Check-In Location: All participants must check in at Woodlawn, regardless of session topic. Timing: Sessions start promptly at 12:00 PM (Sundays). Please arrive early to ensure a timely start. Duration: Approximately 90 minutes. events.description: Did you know that part of the Washington-Rochambeau Revolutionary Route National Historic Trail passes through Prince William Forest Park? Take a hike through history at Prince William Forest Park on the Crossing Trail, which follows part of the route where, in 1781, General Rochambeau's French Army and General Washington's Continental Army marched troops south from New York to fight the British Army in Yorktown, VA during the Revolutionary War. Celebrate the 250th anniversary of American Independence by following in the footsteps of these armies as you learn about travel in the 1700s along this one and a half mile trail. Bring water and bug spray on this mostly shaded one and a half hour hike.

events.description: Join a ranger for a 30-minute, family-friendly walk through Battleground National Cemetery and discover the stories of the soldiers buried here. Learn who these men were and how their service helped shape our nation's history. Uncover clues about the lives of the soldiers, and think about how we remember people who served long ago. Through stories, questions, and observation, children and families will gain a deeper appreciation for the sacrifices made during one of the most important chapters in American history. Perfect for families with children ages 6 and up. This easy walking tour lasts approximately 30 minutes.
